title: Flat, locally finitely presented, separated, locally quasi-finite morphisms with universally bounded fibres are finite locally free on a finite stratification (Stacks 07RY)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], and whose fibres are universally bounded: there is an integer $n\ge0$ such that for every $s\in S$ the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field]) is a finite scheme over $\kappa(s)$, $X_s=\operatorname{Spec}B_s$ with $B_s$ a finite $\kappa(s)$-algebra, of degree $\dim_{\kappa(s)}B_s\le n$ (Stacks Morphisms, Definition 03J4). Then there exist closed subsets $\emptyset=Z_{-1}\subseteq Z_0\subseteq Z_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq Z_n=S$ such that, with $S_r=Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$ for $0\le r\le n$ and $S_r=\emptyset$ for $r>n$, the sets $S_r$ are pairwise disjoint with union $S$, and the following universal property holds: for every morphism of schemes $g:T\to S$ and every integer $r\ge0$, the projection $X\times_ST\to T$ is finite locally free of degree $r$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] if and only if $g(T)\subseteq S_r$ (as sets). (Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RY.)
